sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.89.1 (8ecc2f6), JavaScript, Canvas 2D, Web Audio; AI Hub client 1.4.0 / protocol v1 (35a1047)
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded pixel creatures and luminous violet maze theatre, using native Blob rigs and palette helpers
sourceInformation.animation: Native Blob squash-and-stretch with event-driven mouths, antennae, feet, snack trails and gate choreography
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated electronic score, effects and gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%; human listening unknown
sourceInformation.online: Authoritative shared-world 1–2-player AI Hub co-op, including dedicated hosting and packet-loss repair; standalone solo and simultaneous couch co-op. No standalone matchmaking service.
sourceInformation.testing: One quiet command covers normal legal-input solo/co-op campaigns, 58 generated-board completions, 300 reproducible seeds, final-file Chromium and WebKit, emulated pads/touch, procedural signal checks and official impaired-network/dedicated-host Hub cases; no FPS gate. Physical devices and human listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original rules booklet, contemporary audiovisual description, archived commercial frames and decoded audio signal; exact original audio pitches unknown

testingFeedback: 25 unique findings: 5 exposed by initially failing automated checks and 20 by focused code or visual review; all corrected. Repeated symptoms are counted once.
1 critical issue: the canvas kept its default CSS dimensions, cropping the board and mis-scaling pointer input. Full-viewport sizing and desktop/phone checks verified the fix.

The legal-input whole-campaign playthroughs in the built HTML: solo and co-op each caught all 72 snacks, made all six final catches, reached victory with normal lives and retried cleanly. TV screenshots also exposed the canvas defect.
Static syntax checks caught no gameplay defects and were less informative than actual input, campaign and visual checks.
engineFeedback: The native shaded Blob rig, pixel palette helpers and controller-aware TV Shell gave the game a coherent base.

The native GridMover retains buffered turns and lacks mid-edge reversal; a tested authoritative graph mover supplies the required feel. Explicit controller reassignment also needed input-identity reset.
A deterministic moving-snack maze simulation shared by solo, simultaneous co-op, bots, workshop playtests and Hub authority.
Keeping rotating gates, wrapping edges, continuous motion and swept encounters consistent across route planning and shared state.
No vendored engine changes. Game-specific movement/topology and focused Shell/input adapters extend the engine externally.
Add a dynamic graph-edge mover and a simultaneous shared-world arcade starter with session-safe menus.
promptFeedback: The source-defining moving food, concrete player outcomes and explicit verification gates kept the game coherent.
The proposed first-run duration is a hypothesis: expert legal bots finish much faster, while first-human playtime remains unknown.
Integrating six stages, a complete controller-usable workshop, procedural presentation and authoritative multiplayer into one direct-open HTML.
Separate mandatory acceptance from optional depth, and distinguish measured completion times from desired first-human timing.

aiHub.name: K.C. Chomp Chase
aiHub.description: Hunt twelve runaway snacks while three hungry creatures hunt you. Cut through six mischievous mazes, turn the tables with bright bites, and build a pocket maze of your own.
aiHub.controls: Stick / D-pad / WASD / arrows: steer; south face / Space: reveal; Options / Escape: menu; co-op keyboard: WASD + F, arrows + period.
